clue.text: Lay responsibility on one much obliged

parts.note: to thank someone can mean to hold them responsible, as in 'you have only yourself to thank'
'one' as a pronoun for a person in general can stand for 'you'

explanation.surface: Someone shifts the blame onto a person who is very grateful to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thank' here is the ironic sense of blaming: 'we have the weather to thank for this'. 'One' is the general pronoun, the same as an informal 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'much obliged' is an old-fashioned way of expressing gratitude to someone.

clue.text: One voice in many?

parts.note: many singers sounding together so that they seem to make a single pleasing sound

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes many voices blending agreeably, as if they were one voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical concord is the pleasing combination of several notes or voices sung together.

clue.text: Cocktail of rum and orange: it sticks in the memory

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the two drink words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A rum-and-orange drink so good you will never forget it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocktail of' looks like part of the bar scene but tells you to shuffle the nine letters of RUM and ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: In neuroscience the term names a supposed physical trace left in the brain that stores a memory.

clue.text: Alcohol producer, as in still

indicators.note: the word 'in' shows one piece placed inside another here

parts.note: still means yet, as in 'still waiting'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distiller's still is where alcohol is produced, so the clue sounds like a description of brewing kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' tempts as the distilling vessel, but it is the adverb meaning YET.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungus ferments sugar into alcohol in brewing and winemaking.

clue.text: Performing concerted U-turns? Yes and no

definitions.text: Performing concerted U-turns? Yes and no

indicators.note: performing tricks with the letters means rearranging them into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician keeps making coordinated reversals of policy, which both is and is not reform.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging CONCERTED U-TURNS reconstructs it (the 'yes'), yet the word produced says not reconstructed (the 'no'). In its sense of an unchanged mindset, a person who keeps reversing is the opposite of that.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unchanged in outdated views is called stuck in old ways, the opposite of a politician who keeps reversing.

clue.text: Beginning to buy electronically? It could go to your head

definitions.text: It could go to your head

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, taken here from the word after it

parts.note: doing something electronically is doing it on the net, the internet

explanation.surface: Advice on online shopping: the purchase might go to your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to your head' suggests vanity from buying, but literally means a thing you wear on your head.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat tied under the chin is worn on the head.

clue.text: Refinery waste found around chemical weapon

indicators.note: one word placed around another means it encloses that other word

parts.note: to found a theory is to base it on something
poison gas is a chemical weapon

explanation.surface: Debris at a refinery turns out to surround a chemical weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is not the past tense of find but the verb 'to found', meaning to BASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The dry fibrous residue left after sugar cane is crushed in a sugar refinery is waste.

clue.text: Dope's new in New York

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item about drugs arriving in New York City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs news; it is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Line expurgated from infamous University College poem

indicators.note: infamous here suggests something bad or corrupt, so the letters are put into a disordered arrangement
expurgating removes offending material, so a letter is cut out of the following word

explanation.surface: A scandalous poem from a university college has had a line censored.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one L from COLLEGE ('expurgated from') to leave COLEGE, add U, and rearrange ('infamous') to give the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral verse dialogue of shepherds, like Virgil's, is a kind of short poem.

clue.text: Language Bob perhaps heard in Liverpool?

indicators.note: the Liverpool accent pronounces 'hair' close to 'ur', so the word is said as a Scouser would

parts.note: a bob is one kind of short haircut, a hairstyle

explanation.surface: Bob, a common name, might speak some language in Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a haircut. A Liverpool (Scouse) accent turns the vowel of 'hair' into something like 'ur'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official tongue of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Royal grant wasted with too much claimed?

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grant from the Crown has been squandered by someone claiming too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' signals the shuffle of ROYAL GRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting haughtily means presuming or asserting more importance than is due, claiming too much for oneself.

clue.text: Springy poles designed to sock pigs

indicators.note: designed means made to a plan, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Bouncy poles that were made for hitting pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed' shuffles TO SOCK PIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: These toys are sticks with a spring and footrests that a rider bounces on.

clue.text: Passion for reflection not new in extending practice

indicators.note: not here means the following letter is left out
a reflection in a mirror shows a word backwards

parts.note: Christ's Passion was his agony, so passion means agony

explanation.surface: Thinking about passion for a new activity in which the body is stretched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For reflection' turns AGONY into YNOGA; 'not new' then drops the N.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hindu discipline of stretching postures is a regular exercise routine.

clue.text: Gum may, oddly, repeatedly run hard

indicators.note: taking a word oddly means keeping only its odd-numbered letters
repeatedly means the piece appears twice over

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone chewing gum may run hard again and again in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'may' give MY; 'repeatedly' doubles R.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic resin from a tree is a gum, famously one of the Magi's gifts.

clue.text: Let go and use handle, maybe

indicators.note: maybe means the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: An instruction to release something and use a handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals the shuffle of USE and HANDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Freed from a lead, as a dog might be, means released.

clue.text: High-pressure report?

parts.note: not a weather bulletin but the loud bang caused by a shock wave of compressed air

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-pressure' suggests weather forecasts; 'report' is a loud noise, as of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A supersonic aircraft creates a shock wave of high air pressure heard as an explosive bang.

clue.text: I'm in an old city said to show ill-feeling

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: said means the word is heard as spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: taken as written, then spoken

explanation.surface: Someone in an ancient city shows hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run AN, I'M, O, then the sound of CITY written as SITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or strong dislike is bad feeling.

clue.text: Falls back once more getting half way through race

indicators.note: back means the word is written in reverse

parts.note: once more means again

indicators.note: half of a word means its first half is taken here

explanation.surface: A runner falls back again halfway through a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns AGAIN into NIAGA; the first half of RACE adds RA.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border are known simply by this name.

clue.text: Certain who's out after a fashion

parts.note: certain, as in 'certain people', means some

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word who, with 's as a link

explanation.surface: Someone sure who has gone out in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' shuffles WHO into HOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in some way or other, not clearly, is doing it after a fashion.

clue.text: Plant is nipped by an easterly

indicators.note: nipped by means held between the two other pieces as if pinched

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant is bitten by an east wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nipped by' suggests frost biting a plant, but it is the container signal; 'easterly' gives just the compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mediterranean herb is grown for its seeds with a liquorice flavour.

clue.text: Idiot's reversing round England in automatic

indicators.note: round means placed around another piece, enclosing it
reversing means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person, an idiot; with 's, nuts

explanation.surface: An idiot reverses an automatic car around England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' turns the idiot word into STUN, and 'round' wraps it about England's abbreviation; 'automatic' looks like a car but is a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: This British submachine gun of World War II was an automatic weapon.

clue.text: Potential source of calcium and iron?

definitions.text: Potential source of calcium and iron?

parts.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A dietary question about where to get calcium and iron.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a place serving food could supply those nutrients, and the two chemical symbols spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snack bar serving meals, milk and greens could supply these minerals in your diet.

clue.text: Lady detective buried in the ground

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside another piece
ground means crushed, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A female detective is buried underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The ground' looks like a burial site; 'ground' shuffles THE to ETH, and DI is 'buried in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name is an example of what crosswords mean by lady.

clue.text: Florid mouth cases?

indicators.note: florid means ornate and flowery, so the letters are elaborately rearranged

explanation.surface: Ornate coverings for the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging MOUTH CASES gives the word, and the whole clue describes facial hair framing the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown on the upper lip covers the mouth area.

clue.text: Experience discrimination

definitions.meaning: discrimination as in fine judgement in matters of style

explanation.definitionFit: To get a sample of life is to experience it, and having good aesthetic judgement is having refinement.

clue.text: Sporting special round headdress in Muslim states

indicators.note: round means placed around another piece
sporting means playing about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hat is a headdress

explanation.surface: A sports special edition involving headwear in Islamic countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sporting' rearranges the seven letters of 'special' into CALIPES, and 'round' wraps those about the headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lands ruled by a caliph, an Islamic ruler, are Islamic realms.

clue.text: Door gypsies destroyed outside in a frenzy

indicators.note: with the outside letters destroyed, only an inner stretch of the words remains

explanation.surface: Travellers' doors have been wrecked on the outside in a rampage.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters from DOOR GYPSIES and the run across the word join remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, frenzied bout of indulgence is a debauch.

clue.text: He was caught swinging in tree

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: swinging means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man was caught swinging in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging' shuffles HE WAS into ASHEW.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical tree bears the kidney-shaped nut.

clue.text: Contemplative's in awe of God, finally, leaving for Mass

indicators.note: one letter leaving to make room for another means a swap

parts.note: being in awe of something is dreading it

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A thoughtful person is in awe of God and finally leaves to attend Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: In DREADING the D that is God's last letter makes way for M.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost in reverie or daydreams describes a thoughtful, meditative state.
